summary: A lower bound on the essential radius of an entire purified product set is not coercive: move an epsilon-mass fragment arbitrarily far away and every event probability changes by at most epsilon while the essential radius diverges. Earlier radius-weighted slab inequalities remain valid, but closure must use a slab-conditioned core carrying positive conditional slab mass. The same run proves a tail-insensitive slab-core transfer and applies the newest three-volume density theorem to it.
